$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the unmeasurable branch, and a REAL CAPTURE drives it. The
report declares ten violations in its Total Violations line and attributes none of them to a registry
row, so there is nothing to score recall against. Returning null is what keeps a moved report contract
from reading as 0 of 9 planted defects found, which is the most expensive way to be wrong about the
The report stays at its original path under test/fixtures/test-review-cli/reports/, where the CLI
parser suite already reads it and where the formatters leave captured bytes alone. verdict.json
records why it is not copied here.

storedOutput.capturedBy: a real agent run; test/README.md records that this fixture exists because a real run produced a frontmatter shape every hand-written fixture had missed

derivation: The verdict declares 0 Critical, 0 High, 7 Medium and 3 Low, which sums to 10.
The report has no findings sections at all, so no line matches the Location pattern and no line
matches the Row pattern. Zero findings are attributed.
0 attributed is fewer than 10 declared, so findingsFromReport returns null and scoreVerdict returns
null with it. Nothing about the ground truth enters the arithmetic: the run is unscoreable before the
planted rows are ever consulted, which is why this result stays null even though the report names
files that are not in the eval corpus at all.
The harness that owns this branch treats it as environment-parser and refuses to fold it into a score.
